chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'adab narrated, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isbahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi who said: Al-Mas'oodi narrated to me who said: Al-Hasan ibn Hammad al-Ta'i narrated, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Atiyyah (as he thinks) from Jabir ibn Abdullah who said:

I witnessed Umar at his death saying: 'I repent to God for three things: 1- My dismissal of the slaves of Yemen; 2- My turning back from the army of Usamah after the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had appointed him over us; and 3- Our mutual pledge regarding the people of this House (Ahl al-Bayt), that if God took away His Messenger, we would not appoint any of them.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ: The people of this House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.رَدِّي رَقِيقَ الْيَمَنِ: My dismissal of the slaves of Yemen

ai.seo_question: What were the three things Umar ibn al-Khattab repented for at his death?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this narration as evidence of Umar’s recognition of key Sunni deviations, particularly the delay of Usamah’s expedition which signaled the shift away from the Prophet’s designated leadership. The third regret, concerning the pledge to exclude the Ahl al-Bayt, is interpreted by Shia scholars as an implicit acknowledgment of the right of Ali ibn Abi Talib to succession, contrasting with the eventual establishment of the Caliphate. This confession underscores the theological tension between the immediate command of the Prophet and the political decisions made by the companions during the interim period.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-226 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn al-Hassan al-Mo’adab quoted Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isbahany, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Saqafy, on the authority of Al-Mas’oodi, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Himad al-Ta’ee, on the authority of Zyad ibn al-Monzar, on the authority of Atiye that he thinks that Jabir ibn Abdullah said, “I witnessed that Umar said the following when he faced death: ‘I repent to God for the following three things:

1- Freeing the atheist slaves from Yemen captured by the Muslims;2- Not obeying Usamah whom God’s Prophet (MGB) appointed as the Chief of the Army; and3- We pledged to each other not to let any of the Prophet’s (MGB) family succeed the Prophet (MGB) when God took away his life.’”
